mistakes.note: Vane's dusk ambush never comes: he and four riflemen sit on the spur through the whole raid (M56-M72), the two guards he left with the stock are never seen, two raiders hold the camp and Sefa walks the courier off, and at M96 he is only now 'coming down off the spur'. Against all he said he would do. The round 30 Plot Thread 'now' has him taking the riders from behind, which the page never shows.
Sefa orders 'the third camel's load, the one under the old woman's knot' stripped, though her man searched that load and found nothing and Tamsin's hint to Wren was whispered between the two of them.

A Border Guard trooper finds the raiders his captain was hunting with the Governor's seal broken, never asks where the letters went, tells Hadi he is 'not my business tonight' and binds the robbed courier instead.
The fifth rider with the crossbow is 'the man on it' at M54 and is Sefa, the woman on the bay, from M60.
Jory, who goes barefoot, rolls under the cart and 'his boots came in last'.
The trooper says there are 'four of us at most' and none stood over the salt, against Vane's count at M8: four on the spur with him and two left with the stock.
A dust-rider sits with a carbine and Vane's men carry rifles (M52) in a world where firearms are rare and licensed and Sefa leads with a crossbow.
The move takes the cup and pours the leaking skin out; the reply has the water-wise courier pour it on the ground and be scolded for wasting it, a blunder the move did not ask for.

PC status piles up passing states and repeats (the light going long, light nearly gone, the wrenched shoulder three ways) and records a 'cut' the page never gave; PC looks take 'her arm is bent wrong'.
NPC looks hold carried things and passing states: Sefa's loaded crossbow and where her cloth sits, Hadi's knives and veil up or down, each veil move rewriting the looks and redrawing the portrait.

What NPCs know fills with repeated entries for people off the page who learned nothing (Ossery rounds 15 and 24, Marrick rounds 15 and 42, the Free Wells), and at round 38 Vane 'suspects Tamsin of helping the raiders', which is not his suspicion.

The Plot Thread 'now' says Vane returned at 19:15 and has Tamsin under guard at the Red Teeth, while the same records have Sefa's two riders holding that camp and the page (M96) has Vane still up the spur.
The picked Choice lashes 'the empty skin' when Tamsin had stopped the pour and the skin still held water; the reply has to correct it.

Choices that don't fit who is there: round 40 asks Sefa where to put the salt and camels left behind at the Red Teeth, and rounds 43-44 give Hadi the raider orders as a friend (lead the trooper's horse, carry word to Tamsin).

The summary says Wren's shoulder was hurt when Hadi stopped her at the reins (the horse rode her down at M58), puts the camel's unloading after it lurched into the cart, and leaves the riding-down out.

The Loose End 'Which of Wren or Jory should Tamsin look for when the horses come?' is still open after the raid, and 'What message is the rider carrying ahead to the Well?' was dropped at round 41 with no answer on the page.
The opening picture adds a second old figure in a cap beside Tamsin, has Jory pointing both ways at once, and stands the camels under a canopy the story doesn't have.
The row of goatskin waterskins is drawn as clay jars.
Shows Jory helping Tamsin bind a couched camel, in boots; on the page Wren holds the standing camel and Jory is off at the ring's edge watching the spur.
Wren, in knee-high riding boots on the page, is drawn barefoot here and at M92 and in sandals at M90, and hatless in most scenes.
Hadi is drawn as an older bearded man in a hooded robe, and Wren holds the line in her hands instead of being bound by it.
Both portraits add a scar down the cheek, and the redrawn one wraps her in a linen sling the page never gave her, taken from the 'arm bent wrong' record.
Redrawn for her lowered cloth yet still shows her face covered, and gives a crossbow woman a cartridge belt the page never mentions.

choices.reason: Distinct most rounds and the peg, the seal and the hail bend what follows, but a dozen rounds offer the same satchel and waterskin chores, and a few fit no one (pour the water out, orders for Hadi).

surprise.reason: The raid is signposted from the first page; the riders slipping the ambush, Sefa making Wren break the seal herself and the trooper's arrest land fairly, but the hidden counter-moves (Vane's charge, Tamsin's arrest) never reach the page.

threads.reason: The letters thread strikes at dusk as set, ends in their taking and grows a follow-on; the others only wait, and the hidden 'nows' run out of step with the page.

characters.reason: Tamsin and Sefa are people with voices and wants, but Vane drops his own ambush and the caravan with no cause shown, and his trooper waves the raiders off.

continuity.reason: Vane's six guards fall out of the scene and the trooper's count contradicts his, with smaller slips (Jory's boots, the crossbow rider's sex, a carbine).

pacing.reason: Twenty-five rounds spend two hours of story time passing the satchel and the skins back and forth before dusk; from the raid on every reply moves, but the road never does.

prose.reason: Vivid, concrete and in one dry voice, marred by tics (the wrenched shoulder burning down to her fingers, mouths going flat, light the colour of things), speech lines left unmarked and a few garbled ones.

pictures.reason: Faces and Tamsin's dress hold well and the places are right, but over half the scenes carry a wrong detail: an extra figure, jars for skins, Wren barefoot, Hadi as an old man, a sling and scar on Wren's portrait.

secrets.reason: Nothing the threads hide is told; Ossery and the man in Kesh come only as fair hints, with one crossing where Sefa names the satchel's hiding place.

agency.reason: Wren does what the move gave and no more, the Continue leaves her deciding nothing; one reply reads a move as a blunder.

stakes.reason: Every risk from the raid on is checked; failures cost a wrenched shoulder, the knife, her freedom and a hanging charge, all carried forward, and the successes are won by what she said.

state.reason: Time, place, journal, lore and the bench's actions hold, but PC status and looks, NPC looks and knowledge, Plot Thread nows, Loose Ends, the summary and some Choices are stale or wrong, one reaching a portrait.

adventure.reason: Danger is met in action and at a real cost at the Red Teeth, ridden down, a knife at the throat, marched off and made to break the seal, but the whole run stays at one halt, the road never moves, and Sefa and the trooper decide how Wren gets through.

violence.reason: Being ridden down by a horse and having the hurt arm twisted are clear and physical, with the shoulder's pain carried on, but each is quick and nothing bleeds.
